# Opt-In Cloud Fallback

A remote model call that is **structurally optional**: absent a key it does not exist, present a key it
fires only for inputs a cheap local gate has already judged novel, and on any failure it degrades to
the local answer rather than to an error. The counterpart of [[on-device-first-inference]].

The distinguishing test is what happens with the network unplugged and no credentials. If the feature
disappears and the product still works, the fallback is genuinely opt-in. In [[farely]] it is:

> "This is a deliberate, documented departure from \"nothing leaves the phone\": a screen capture
> leaves the device **only** for this classifier, and only for screens that pass a cheap on-device
> novelty gate."
> — Farley/docs/VISION.md, 2026-07-13

## The four gates, in order

1. **No key ⇒ no call.** `classifyScreen(capture, apiKey)` returns `heuristicClassify()` immediately.
   The key comes from Settings and lives in `localStorage` only — never committed, never bundled.
2. **Event-type gate.** Only `WINDOW_STATE_CHANGED` is eligible; content churn inside a screen is not.
3. **Novelty gate.** A PL/EN keyword list (`NOVELTY_HINTS`: update / aktualiz / wersj / regulamin / …)
   must match. It **deliberately omits every verification term**:

   > "Deliberately excludes verification/selfie terms: identity checks are detected on-device by the
   > coordinator and NEVER routed to cloud vision."
   > — Farley/apps/android/.../FarelyAccessibilityService.kt, 2026-07-13

4. **Throttle and freeze.** At most one call per platform per 5 minutes, and `if
   (MultiAppCoordinator.frozen) return` runs before any of it.

## Failure semantics

Failure is *silence plus a diagnostics row*, not a dialog. A refused, timed-out or malformed response
falls back to `heuristicClassify()`, and the result carries `VisionResult.method: "cloud" |
"on-device"` so downstream code and the driver can both tell which answer they are looking at — the
[[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]] habit applied to inference. Every call is logged as a `vision`
event in [[on-device-black-box-diagnostics]].

## The residual risk, stated

The exclusion of identity screens is enforced by a **keyword list**, not by the type system or the
platform. A verification screen whose text happens to contain a novelty word the list misses could
still be captured and sent. Farely documents the intent in four places but cannot structurally
guarantee it; the honest claim is "heuristic, biased towards false-positive freezing", and that is what
belongs on the record.
